channel.title: Justin Erasmus blog
channel.description: Practical AI, automation and hybrid music from South Africa

item.title: The 808 was “not real drums”: what music's tech panics tell us about AI
item.description: From the TR-808 and Sousa's “mechanical music” warning to synthesizers, samplers and Pro Tools: every tool that changed music was first written off as fake. Where AI fits in that pattern, and where it doesn't.

item.title: Not slop: what human-led AI music production actually involves
item.description: “AI slop” means content where nobody is steering. Here is where the human decisions sit in a Prismatic Wave record, and where critics of AI music have a point.

item.title: If listeners can't tell, labels matter: AI-music disclosure in South Africa
item.description: Most listeners can't tell AI music from human music by ear, and South Africa's rulebook is still being written. What honest disclosure to rights bodies and listeners could look like.

item.title: What I learned releasing 37 human + AI records in 13 months
item.description: A data-first look at the Prismatic Wave catalogue: 37 releases and 152 tracks on Apple Music between February 2025 and March 2026, and what the process taught me.

item.title: When AI wrote the AI policy: lessons for every South African business
item.description: South Africa's draft AI policy was withdrawn after AI-generated errors. Here's what small businesses can learn about checking AI output.

item.title: The 4-Stage Framework behind Prismatic Wave
item.description: How Prismatic Wave records are made: the AlgoRythm 4-Stage Hybrid Music Framework of Concept, Generation, Human Curation and Production & Delivery.

item.title: South Africa's AI music rulebook is blank: what independent artists should know
item.description: SAMRO wants AI disclosure, the SABC has no final policy on AI-assisted music, and the Suno lawsuits continue. A practical guide for independent South African artists.
